author: NorthEast News Desk
body: U.S. stocks were lower in midday trading Monday as concerns about artificial-intelligence spending weighed on technology shares, Reuters reported. At 11:40 a.m. Eastern, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.23%, the S&P 500 had fallen 0.42% and the Nasdaq Composite was down 0.44%.

Nvidia was down about 3%, while Amazon fell more than 1%. Intel, AMD and Marvell were each down roughly 5% to 6% in the snapshot. The moves showed how quickly investor expectations around AI demand and competition can spread across both chipmakers and the large companies buying or building AI capacity.

Oil prices were also higher in the report, adding another variable for investors to weigh. The figures are a mid-session reading from Reuters and are not closing prices or a live quote after publication; markets can move materially before the trading day ends.
The session’s direction was not a final verdict on the technology sector, but it showed how concentrated AI exposure can amplify a market pullback.
dek: U.S. stocks were lower in a midday snapshot as Nvidia and several semiconductor names fell amid renewed concern about the pace and payoff of AI investment.
headline: Wall Street slides as AI anxiety pressures Nvidia and chip stocks
